site.name: prelaps
home.title: prelaps — free browser tools
home.description: Free tools that run in your browser: fix garbled text, resize images in bulk, settle who goes first. No sign-up, no uploads, nothing leaves your device.
home.heading: Tools that run in your browser
home.intro: New ones get added whenever I need them. All of them work without an account, entirely in your browser.
tools.mojibake.name: Mojibake Fixer
tools.mojibake.desc: Recover text that turned into garbled characters after being saved or opened with the wrong encoding — EUC-KR read as UTF-8, and other common mismatches.
tools.imagesquish.name: Bulk Image Resizer
tools.imagesquish.desc: Resize a whole batch at once, convert to WebP, JPEG or PNG, and take it as a zip. Nothing is uploaded, so there is no cap on size or count.
tools.race.name: Race Roulette
tools.race.desc: Type in names and watch them race. Decide lunch, chores, or who pays — the finish order is your result, and weights show up as boosters you can watch rather than hidden odds.
about.title: About prelaps
about.description: Who builds prelaps, what gets built and what does not, and how your data is handled.
about.heading: About
about.lede: prelaps is a small personal site for tools that run in your browser. No account, no install, nothing uploaded.
about.who.p: One person builds and runs it. Not a company and not a team — the idea, the code, the writing and the three translations all come from the same desk. Tools do not appear quickly because of that. What is here, though, is what I keep using myself, so when something breaks I notice and fix it.
about.why.p1: The first tool was the mojibake fixer. I reopened a CSV I had filed away a few years earlier and every name in it had turned into unreadable symbols. The recovery sites I found all wanted the file uploaded, and it was work material, so I could not. I ended up building one that finishes inside the browser instead.
about.why.p2: It has gone the same way since. I need something, nothing suitable exists, I build it and leave it here. The bulk image resizer and the race picker used for settling turns both arrived that way.
about.local.p1: There is no server behind these tools. Whatever you paste or pick is processed inside your browser and never leaves your device. That is less a promise than a structure — there is nothing at the other end to receive it.
about.local.p2: It has practical consequences. With no upload there is no reason to cap file size or count, and no queue to wait in; in exchange, speed follows whatever machine you are on. The one program you download (VFilemanage) is the exception, and it too runs only on your own PC.
about.pick.h: What gets built and what does not
about.pick.p: Only things I have gone looking for more than once. If something good already exists I do not rebuild it, and I do not pad the site with calculators and unit converters to catch searches. The same reasoning is why every tool page says where that tool stops working — knowing the cases it cannot fix saves you the attempt.
about.ads.p1: The domain and hosting are paid for personally, and ads cover the cost. They go where they do not sit over an input box or a run button, and using the tools stays free and unconditional.
about.ads.p2: Google Analytics is used to count visits. What that does and does not record is set out here —
about.contact.p: Something broken, a wrong result, a feature you wish existed — any of it helps. This is a one-person project, so a reply can take a few days. The address is here —

privacy.title: Privacy Policy | prelaps
privacy.description: What prelaps collects, what it does not, and how each tool handles what you enter.
privacy.heading: Privacy Policy
privacy.intro: This policy covers prelaps (prelaps.com) and every tool published on it.
privacy.s1.p1: prelaps has no sign-up and no account, and asks for no personal details such as a name or an email address. Cookies are used for visit statistics and advertising, which section 2 below covers separately.
privacy.s1.p2: Whatever you type or upload is processed entirely inside your browser. This is not only a promise in a document — the site has no server that receives your text. Closing or reloading the page discards it, and no browser storage is used, so nothing is left on your device either.
privacy.s1.p3: Accordingly the following are never collected: name, email address, phone number, account details, the contents of anything you type or upload, or file names.
privacy.analytics.p1: The site uses Google Analytics 4. It shows how often each page is opened, and whether a tool is merely looked at or actually used. That is what decides which one gets worked on next.
privacy.analytics.p2: Tool usage events carry only values that keep no content — a length bucket, an output format. Text you paste, file names and file contents are not sent. They never leave your device in the first place, so there is nothing to send.
privacy.analytics.p3: Google Analytics distinguishes repeat visits using cookies and comparable identifiers. Blocking cookies in your browser, or installing the opt-out add-on Google provides, stops the collection.
privacy.analytics.link.partner: How Google uses data from sites that use its services
privacy.ads.p1: The site serves ads through Google AdSense. During the review period the slots may not be filled yet and can appear blank.
privacy.ads.p2: Google and other third-party vendors use cookies to serve ads based on your prior visits to this site and to other sites on the web.
privacy.ads.p3: Personalised advertising can be switched off. Google Ad Settings turns off personalisation for Google’s own ads; aboutads.info turns it off across many participating vendors at once.
privacy.fonts.p: Some pages load their typeface from Google Fonts, so opening them sends a request to fonts.googleapis.com and fonts.gstatic.com. Your IP address and browser type may reach Google as part of that request. Only the connection information needed to deliver the font is involved — nothing you typed is included.
privacy.logs.p: The site is served as static files by a hosting provider, which may keep ordinary access logs — IP address, timestamp, requested path — for operation and troubleshooting. The operator does not use these logs to identify individual visitors.
privacy.children.p: The site is not directed at children under 14, and no personal information is collected from visitors of any age.
privacy.rights.p: Because no personal information is stored, there is nothing to request access to, correct, or delete. If you believe otherwise, please get in touch.
privacy.contact.p: Questions about this policy can be sent to
privacy.changes.p: Any change to this policy is reflected on this page together with the date. Changes that actually widen what is collected — introducing advertising or analytics, for example — are written here before they take effect.
privacy.s3.intro: Each tool is listed with what it collects, why, how long it is kept, and whether anything is shared. These answers are about what you put into the tool, and they are currently the same for all of them. Site-wide visit statistics and advertising are in section 2.
privacy.tool.mojibake.note: Pasted text and uploaded files are decoded in the browser and are never sent anywhere.
privacy.tool.imagesquish.note: Images you drop in are processed inside the browser and never sent to a server. Neither are their filenames.
privacy.tool.race.name: Race Picker
privacy.tool.race.note: Names and weights you enter stay in the page. Refreshing clears them.

terms.description: The conditions for using prelaps and the tools published on it.
terms.heading: Terms of Use
terms.intro: These terms cover prelaps (prelaps.com) and every tool published on it.
terms.what.p: A set of free browser tools run by one person. There is no sign-up, no stored user data, and all processing happens in your browser.
terms.noWarranty.p1: These tools estimate, sort, and transform — they do not certify. Results can be wrong, and each tool page describes where that tool tends to fail.
terms.noWarranty.p2: Keep your own copy of anything that matters before replacing it with a result from here. The operator is not responsible for loss that follows from overwriting an original.
terms.duty.p1: Anyone may use these tools. Please avoid:

terms.duty.li2: Copying the site wholesale and redistributing it as your own
terms.duty.p2: You keep the rights to, and the responsibility for, whatever you enter. The operator cannot see it.
terms.change.p: This is a free service provided by an individual. Features may change and the service may stop without notice, with no obligation to compensate.
terms.liability.p: To the extent permitted by law, the operator is not liable for direct or indirect damages arising from the use of, or inability to use, these tools. They are provided as is.
terms.law.p: These terms are governed by the laws of the Republic of Korea.

contact.title: Contact | prelaps
contact.description: How to reach the person who runs prelaps.
contact.heading: Contact
contact.email.p: Bug reports, suggestions, and questions about privacy or the terms all go to the same address.
contact.email.note: This is a one-person project, so a reply can take a few days.
contact.report.p: Please say which tool you were using and what you expected to happen. If a tool produced a wrong result, the input that caused it helps most.
contact.report.warn: Please do not send sensitive files. The tools never upload your files, and they are not needed to reproduce a report either.
contact.before.p: Each tool page has a section on where that tool commonly fails. A fair share of reports turn out to be cases the tool cannot fix, because the original information is already gone.
tools.vfile.name: VFilemanage
tools.vfile.desc: Gather files buried deep in folders into one place and open the originals on double-click. Nothing is moved. A Windows program you download and install.
privacy.tool.vfile.note: This page only provides information and download links. Once downloaded, the program runs entirely on your own PC, and what you organise and your settings are stored in your user folder on that PC. The download buttons lead to GitHub, where GitHub's own policy applies.
home.find.lede: Which tool you need usually follows from the symptom in front of you. Pick the closest one.
home.find.s1.q: I opened a CSV in Excel and the names came out as ë³´ê³ ì„œ
home.find.s1.a: The file itself is almost certainly fine. It was saved as UTF-8 without the marker that says so, and Excel fell back to a legacy code page. Adding that marker, a BOM, and downloading again makes it open correctly.
home.find.s2.q: I unzipped an archive and only the filenames are garbled. The contents are fine
home.find.s2.a: A zip stores names and contents separately. An older archiver left the flag that says the names are UTF-8 empty, so your computer read them with a different table. The compressed data was never touched, so only the names need rewriting.
home.find.s3.q: I want to paste garbled text out of an email and get it back on the spot
home.find.s3.a: Paste it in and the tool works out which tables were mismatched, then lays out the candidates. Nothing to upload, and no need to know the encoding beforehand.
home.find.s4.q: I want to understand why this keeps happening in the first place
home.find.s4.a: Latin letters keep almost the same number in every table, but Korean and Japanese characters differ in both number and byte length. Pick the wrong table and even the character count stops lining up.
home.find.s5.q: I have dozens of photos to shrink for a blog post and convert to WebP
home.find.s5.a: Set size, format and quality on one screen, run them all at once, and take the results as a zip. There is no upload, so no cap on file size or count.
home.find.s6.q: I want to settle who pays or who presents first, in front of everyone
home.find.s6.a: Type in names and a race decides the order. Weights show up as boosters you can watch rather than hidden odds, and a result everyone watched lands better than being told the computer picked.
home.find.s7.q: My files are buried in deep folders and I want to open them from one place
home.find.s7.a: Keep the ones you open often in a single list and double-click to launch the original. Nothing is moved or copied. This one is a Windows program you download and install.
home.read.lede: For when you would rather understand the cause before opening a tool. A fair number of these turn out not to need the tool at all.
home.faq.q1: Is it really free? Do I need an account?
home.faq.a1: Everything is free, with no account and no sign-in. There are no usage limits and nothing turns paid later. Domain and hosting costs are covered by ads.
home.faq.q2: Do my files get sent to a server?
home.faq.a2: They do not. That is less a promise than a matter of structure, since there is no server here to receive them. If you want to check, open your browser's network tab and run a file through. Nothing goes out.
home.faq.q3: Is there a limit on file size or count?
home.faq.a3: None is set. The caps free tools usually put up, 50MB and the like, come from server costs, and nothing here passes through someone else's server. The real limit is your device's memory.
home.faq.q4: Do these work on a phone?
home.faq.a4: Every browser-based tool here works on a phone. The processing power comes from your device, though, so large jobs like hundreds of photos finish faster on a computer. VFilemanage is the exception, being a Windows program.
home.faq.q5: Do they work without an internet connection?
home.faq.a5: Once a page is open it keeps working if the connection drops, because nothing is handed to a server. You will need a connection again after a refresh or once the tab is closed.
home.faq.q6: What if the result is wrong?
home.faq.a6: These tools make an informed guess. Very short pieces of garbled text give them little to go on, and that is where they fail most often. Each tool page spells out where it stops working. Keep an original copy of anything important, and reporting a wrong result genuinely helps.
articles.encodingBasics.title: UTF-8 and legacy encodings, explained
articles.encodingBasics.desc: Starts from how computers store letters as numbers and works up to why a mismatch produces shapes like ¾È³çÇÏ¼¼¿ä. Written to be readable without knowing what an encoding is.
articles.excelCsv.title: When a CSV comes out garbled in Excel
articles.excelCsv.desc: Why the same file looks fine in a text editor, what those three BOM bytes actually do, and what to do in the opposite case where the file really is in a legacy encoding.
articles.zipFilename.title: When filenames inside a zip are garbled
articles.zipFilename.desc: Why the names break while the contents do not, why it often shows up only on a Mac or a differently localized Windows, and how to rewrite the names without unpacking the archive.
articles.imageSizes.title: What size should you resize to — blog, thumbnail, OG image
articles.imageSizes.desc: Recommended dimensions per use and where those numbers come from. The rule is twice the displayed width, and the OG image is the one exception.
articles.fairDraw.title: How to run a draw people will accept
articles.fairDraw.desc: Where ladder lotteries, spinning wheels and random-pick buttons hold up and where they fall apart, plus the arithmetic for applying weights honestly.
articles.organize.title: Organizing files without moving them
articles.organize.desc: Shortcuts, Windows libraries, symbolic links and search compared, with the limits of each. It starts with what moving a file quietly breaks.
guides.title: Reading | prelaps
guides.description: Garbled text, image dimensions, fair draws, organizing files. Articles for when you would rather understand the cause before opening a tool.
guides.heading: Reading
guides.lede: Every tool here has a point where it stops working. Knowing that boundary before you start saves a lot of wasted attempts, and these articles were written to explain it.
guides.why: Often enough, understanding the cause means you no longer need the tool. A CSV garbled in Excel is usually a missing marker rather than a broken file, and how far to shrink a photo comes down to a single rule.
articles.notepadUtf8.title: Saved as UTF-8 in Notepad and it still came out garbled
articles.notepadUtf8.desc: Why picking the right option was not enough. What ANSI actually means, when the default changed, and when a BOM helps versus breaks things.
articles.imageQuality.title: What quality setting should you use — why 0.8 is the default
articles.imageQuality.desc: What the slider actually discards, why the returns bend at 0.8, and where photos, screenshots and noisy images each diverge.
articles.drawMany.title: When you need more than one pick — groups and running order
articles.drawMany.desc: Picking one name and settling an order are different problems. Drawing without repeats, two ways to split groups, and what to do past twelve people.
articles.notABackup.title: Organizing is not backing up
articles.notABackup.desc: Where the feeling that organized means safe breaks down. Why sync is not a backup, the 3-2-1 rule, and how to run both together.
tools.doceditor.name: HWP & Ichitaro Document Editor
tools.doceditor.desc: Open HWP, HWPX and Ichitaro (JTD) forms in your browser without Hancom Office or Ichitaro, fill in the blanks, and save them in the same format. Photos and signatures supported.
privacy.tool.doceditor.note: Documents you open and the photos or signatures you add are processed inside the browser and never sent to a server. Saved files are downloaded straight to your device.
tools.idphoto.name: ID Photo Size Fitter
tools.idphoto.desc: Crop a photo you already have to passport or résumé dimensions, set the print resolution, and fit a file size limit. Covers Korean, U.S. and Japanese sizes.
privacy.tool.idphoto.note: The photo you open is handled inside your browser and is never sent to a server. The cropped result is downloaded straight from this device.
